title: Cipla Limited shows an absence of surviving findings after rigorous examination of filed results
abstract: Every explanation we tested for the change was either rejected or weakened, so no finding survives as detailed in Table 3. This research note examines Cipla Limited, a pharmaceutical manufacturer listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, as of 16 October 2026. We focus on growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier, compared against 4 listed peers. Revenue from operations in Q1 FY27 was Rs 6,142.0 crore and EBITDA margin was 25.0 per cent in Q1 FY27. Growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier stood at 8.4 per cent in Q1 FY27. Before Q3 FY26 it had averaged 3.5 per cent, and the clearest break is in Q3 FY26. Receivable days grew faster than revenue over the last four quarters, suggesting channel stuffing ahead of a pricing change, which weakened and the checks applied to it were not conclusive either way. India branded formulations revenue substituting for US generics decline was rejected because the move is sector-wide, not company-specific. The measure to watch is growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier in the next results.
introduction: This note focuses on growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier, compared against 4 listed peers. We examine the pharmaceutical manufacturer Cipla Limited, which is listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, as of 16 October 2026.
company_and_data: Revenue from operations in Q1 FY27 was Rs 6,142.0 crore [1]. A year earlier, in Q1 FY26, it was Rs 5,467.0 crore. EBITDA margin was 25.0 per cent in Q1 FY27. We examined 8 quarters of filed results. Table 1 shows revenue from operations rose from Rs 5,201.0 crore in Q2 FY25 to Rs 6,142.0 crore in Q1 FY27. Table 2 presents margins and revenue growth, computed from Table 1. Table 4 shows the latest comparable quarter across the company and its listed peers. Figure 1 illustrates quarterly revenue and EBITDA, Q2 FY25 to Q1 FY27, in Rs crore.
findings: Growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier stood at 8.4 per cent in Q1 FY27. Before Q3 FY26 it had averaged 3.5 per cent. The clearest break is in Q3 FY26. Figure 2 shows US revenue growth, year on year, in USD at Cipla Limited rose over the quarters examined from Q3 FY26.
explanations: Receivable days grew faster than revenue over the last four quarters, suggesting channel stuffing ahead of a pricing change, which weakened. The checks applied to it were not conclusive either way. India branded formulations revenue is substituting for US generics decline was rejected. The move is sector-wide, not company-specific. According to Table 3, every explanation we tested for the change was either rejected or weakened, so no finding survives.
outlook: The measure to watch is growth in US revenue measured in US dollars, on the same quarter a year earlier in the next results.
conclusion: Every explanation we tested for the change was either rejected or weakened, so no finding survives as documented in Table 3. We evaluated the filed results and market comparisons for Cipla Limited as of 16 October 2026 without finding surviving explanations for the observed operational shifts.
